newsitem.title: USA: Greenspan Q&A -- Part III, CPI, economic growth.
newsitem.headline: Greenspan Q&A -- Part III, CPI, economic growth.

text.p: Following are excerpts from the question and answer session of Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan before the House Banking Monetary Policy subcommittee on Wednesday.
Greenspan delivered the second and final leg of his Humphrey-Hawkins address at 1400 EST/1900 GMT.

GREENSPAN: "There's a lot of volatility in the markets. Markets will move on rumors. They will move on statements by myself or my colleagues. But what you cannot do is affect the underlying forces. You can do it on a daily basis. You try to do it more than that, you will fail."

Rep. FRANK: "I was pleased to hear your articulation that your concern on the CPI is with its goal as a measure for use in the economy. The fact, I gather, is that the news is even better than the number might look because to the extent the CPI overstates inflation then there is less inflation in the economy than that low number shows.

"I also take it that what you're saying is that you express no opinion then on whether or not we should be reducing the cost of living adjustment. You are not expressing any opinion that we are over-compensating Social Security recipients as a matter of policy."
GREENSPAN: "That's correct."
FRANK: "If we were to decide that low-income should be treated separately and that the CPI calculation should be separate, that's not a problem for you?
GREENSPAN: "Correct."
FRANK: "Two other points. One, you conclude by saying you're going to conclude on an upbeat note. You upbeat is most people depressed, you realize?

"What I'm concerned about is ... it does seem to me that over the years you have been somewhat pleasantly surprised that we've had as steady growth and as great a reduction in unemployment as we've had with so little inflation. Am I correct that you were somewhat pleasantly surprised in that your expectations were somewhat more pessimistic over the last few years?"
GREENSPAN: "That's correct, Congressman."

FRANK: "I think that's a factor, because what some of us are worried about when you talk about pre-emptive strikes that you might be a little too pre-emptive because there has been this historic mis-estimate. And a lot people missed it.

"I recall asking you your view of the effect of the tax increase of late 1993. You said you did believe it would have a negative effect on the economy. I guess the question is, do you still believe the tax increases of 1993 had a negative effect on growth? And the second part of the question is, if they did, and growth would have been even higher, wouldn't that have meant you'd have been more restrictive?"

GREENSPAN: "It is certainly the case that the economy is doing exceptionally well from our point of view -- not from yours. It's almost certainly the case that there is no direct evidence that you can see that capital investment or anything has been slowed down.
"It's very hard for me to believe that when you increase marginal rates it has no effect. But there are so many other things going on in the economy that it's hard to disentangle.
"So, all I can say to you is that the hypothesis that it had a demonstrable negative effect is not capable of being proved."
FRANK: "To the extent that your view was correct that the tax increases of 1993 did slow the economy down, is it not the case that had that not happened you would have been more restrictive?"
GREENSPAN: "Not necessarily. It's hard to tell what would have happened in the context of inflation.
"It wasn't growth per se that we find is something we respond to. It's evidences of inflationary imbalances which upend the economy. But it's not growth per se."
FRANK: "The fact that the unemployment rate could drop further and growth could continue is in itself no reason for people to get nervous or to make pre-emptive strikes?"
GREENSPAN: "I want you to understand that a very substantial part of the academic community does believe that. I am very skeptical of that relationship myself."
(( -- N.A. Treasury Desk, 212-859-1660 ))
